title: Matrix multiplication — 2×2 product AB
question:
**Matrix Multiplication.** Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$.

Compute the product $AB$ by finding each entry as a row-by-column dot product. Give the complete resulting $2 \times 2$ matrix.

solution_steps.title: Understand the Setup
solution_steps.description:
Matrix multiplication works by pairing each **row of $A$** with each **column of $B$** and taking a dot product — meaning we multiply matching entries and add the results.

For two $2 \times 2$ matrices, the result $AB$ is also a $2 \times 2$ matrix where entry $(i, j)$ = (row $i$ of $A$) $\cdot$ (column $j$ of $B$).

There are exactly **4 entries** to compute, one for each $(i,j)$ combination: $(1,1),\ (1,2),\ (2,1),\ (2,2)$.

solution_steps.title: Assemble the Result
solution_steps.description:
Place the four computed entries into their correct positions:
$$AB = \begin{pmatrix} (1,1) & (1,2) \\ (2,1) & (2,2) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 36 \\ 3 & 30 \end{pmatrix}$$

title: Right-triangle trig — height from angle and hypotenuse
question:
**Right-Triangle Trigonometry.** A 35-ft wire is attached from the top of a vertical antenna straight down to a stake in the level ground, forming a $58°$ angle with the ground.

To the nearest tenth of a foot, how tall is the antenna? Show which trigonometric ratio you used and set up the equation before solving.

solution_steps.title: Understand the Setup
solution_steps.description:
A wire stretches from the **top of a vertical antenna** to a **stake in the ground**, making a $58°$ angle with the ground. This creates a right triangle where:
- The **wire** (35 ft) is the **hypotenuse** — it's the longest side, stretching from stake to antenna top
- The **antenna** is the **opposite side** — it's directly across from the $58°$ angle
- The **ground** is the **adjacent side** — it runs along the bottom

The key question becomes: which trig ratio connects the **opposite** side and the **hypotenuse**?

solution_steps.title: Choose the Trig Ratio
solution_steps.description:
**SOH–CAH–TOA** tells us:
$$\sin(\theta) = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$$

With $\theta = 58°$, the opposite side is the antenna height $h$, and the hypotenuse is the 35-ft wire — both pieces we need are connected by **sine**.

Set up the equation:
$$\sin(58°) = \frac{h}{35}$$

solution_steps.title: Solve for h
solution_steps.description:
Multiply both sides by 35 to isolate $h$:
$$h = 35 \times \sin(58°)$$

Evaluating $\sin(58°) \approx 0.8480$:
$$h = 35 \times 0.8480 \approx 29.68 \text{ ft}$$

Rounded to the nearest tenth: $h \approx 29.7$ ft.

title: Multi-step linear equation with fractions
question:
**Multi-Step Linear Equation.** Solve for $x$:
$$3(2x - 5) - 4(x + 1) = \frac{x + 7}{2} + 1$$
Show each step clearly and give your answer as a simplified fraction or integer.

solution_steps.title: Understand the Problem
solution_steps.description:
We have a linear equation with parentheses on the left and a fraction on the right. The game plan is:
1. **Expand** all parentheses to clear the grouping symbols.
2. **Simplify** each side independently.
3. **Eliminate the fraction** by multiplying through.
4. **Isolate** $x$.

Key thing to watch: the subtraction sign in front of $-4(x+1)$ distributes to **both** terms inside — a common place to slip up.

solution_steps.title: Expand Left Side
solution_steps.description:
Distribute each coefficient into its parentheses:
$$3(2x - 5) = 6x - 15$$
$$-4(x + 1) = -4x - 4$$

So the left side becomes:
$$6x - 15 - 4x - 4$$

Combining like terms ($6x - 4x$ and $-15 - 4$):
$$= 2x - 19$$

solution_steps.title: Simplify Right Side
solution_steps.description:
Combine $ rac{x+7}{2} + 1$ into a single fraction by writing $1 =  rac{2}{2}$:
$$ rac{x+7}{2} +  rac{2}{2} =  rac{x + 9}{2}$$

The equation now reads:
$$2x - 19 =  rac{x + 9}{2}$$

solution_steps.title: Eliminate the Fraction
solution_steps.description: Multiply **every term** on both sides by $2$ to clear the denominator:\n$$2 \cdot (2x - 19) = 2 \cdot \frac{x+9}{2}$$\n$$4x - 38 = x + 9$$

solution_steps.title: Isolate $x$
solution_steps.description:
Subtract $x$ from both sides:
$$3x - 38 = 9$$

Add $38$ to both sides:
$$3x = 47$$

Divide both sides by $3$:
$$x =  rac{47}{3}$$

Since $47$ and $3$ share no common factors, this fraction is already fully simplified.

solution_steps.title: Verify the Answer
solution_steps.description:
Substitute $x =  rac{47}{3}$ back into the original equation to confirm.

**Left side:**
$$3\!\left(2 \cdot  rac{47}{3} - 5ight) - 4\!\left( rac{47}{3} + 1ight)$$
$$= 3\!\left( rac{94}{3} -  rac{15}{3}ight) - 4\!\left( rac{50}{3}ight)$$
$$= 3 \cdot  rac{79}{3} -  rac{200}{3} = 79 -  rac{200}{3} =  rac{237 - 200}{3} =  rac{37}{3}$$

**Right side:**
$$ rac{ rac{47}{3} + 7}{2} + 1 =  rac{ rac{68}{3}}{2} + 1 =  rac{68}{6} + 1 =  rac{34}{3} +  rac{3}{3} =  rac{37}{3}$$

✅ Both sides equal $\dfrac{37}{3}$.
